title: The Imaginary Invalid by Molière adapted by Bill Irwin on Broadway #t...
transcript: On paper, this 90-minute Molière production with comics like Rachel Bloom and Bill Irwin should be a knee-slapper, but it somehow falls flat. The eccentric hypochondriac Argan is determined to marry his daughter into a family of doctors, overlooking her true love, the handsome Cleante, for a weirdo with a tragic bowl cut. There's also a side plot involving Argan's gold-digging wife and a funny dynamic between him and his servant Toinette, all painting him as an absolute buffoon. This production gives you the physicality and the over-the-top delivery that makes Molière so charming, but the bigger picture is missing. Any intellectual satire that could inject some depth into the piece is completely buried, leaving it thin and distant. It's a very safe and by the book telling of a story that's humorous, but not inherently eventful enough to sustain 90 minutes. Not to say that this is a poorly done production — the performances and the ensemble work are enjoyable, and I certainly did laugh, but those laughs felt a little too surface-level. Had I already been familiar with the play, I'm not sure how much mileage I would have gotten out of it.
reasoning: Reviewer acknowledges enjoyable performances and some laughs but criticizes the production as flat, surface-level, and lacking depth, questioning its value for repeat viewers.
